pr_body:
This creates an abstraction for `ResourceLoader` and `ResourceFormatLoader` to load cyclic resources, ie. ressources currently loading that normally returns a null `Resource` when queried.

Supersedes #71004
Fixes #70985
Fixes #71610
pr_comments:
I am still not convinced in the approach or whether this a problem, if you cyclic preloads() with scenes, then you will not be able to easily free them eventually. I think its correct that it fails and should not be fixed.

The error you receive should let you know that this is a problem and that you should use load() instead and take care of properly freeing this scene manually to break the cyclic link.

@adamscott Circular reference for scripts should be valid to some extent, because you can have a reference to the parser code (at least how it was meant to be implemented when we discussed about this with @vnen) however cyclic reference for resources is not because its way too difficult to fix and *extremely* error prone. As such the use case described in the linked issue should always be considered a bug.

Creating code that checks scripts and see if they contain cyclical references and eventually break them is not very difficult, because all you have to do is eliminate the scripts from the objects that contain it and were marked as unused (hence the cyclical link breaks and the objects are freed).

Extending this to the whole resource system is extremely inefficient and would force users to have to do this check for cyclical inclusion errors constantly when instead you can just prevent them on load.
Closing this PR. The GDScript team will have to discuss how to fix this issue otherwise, taking @reduz comments into account.

issue_context.title: Key Scene "Forgets" Its Script on Project Reload
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0 Beta 13 - Also occurred on 4.0 Beta 10

### System information

Windows 11, RTX 3070, AMD Ryzen 7 2700X

### Issue description

Hi everyone!

I've recently started experiencing a _very_ frustrating issue where one of my key scenes (Player Actor) seems to "forget" it has a script on it every time the project is reloaded. 

No matter how many times I save this scene, as soon as I reload the project the script is no longer attached and I need to set everything up again just for that session before it's all forgotten again on next load. The problem briefly went away when I saved the scene again under a new name, but it has just reoccurred, and I suspect this will only become more aggravating should the project get any bigger.

I have made absolutely sure the project and its contents are not read-only - I appreciate this could be my hardware's fault, but as it's this particular scene that keeps malfunctioning under numerous different names, I wonder if the issue is coming from elsewhere.

![2023-01-18 11_32_41-Actor_PlayerN tscn - SoulslikeEngine - Godot Engine](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/106239192/213164024-dd86f6d2-ce0b-47ac-b8e4-cc054b3e2bb5.jpg)

(Before reload)

![2023-01-18 11_33_11-(_) Actor_PlayerN tscn - SoulslikeEngine - Godot Engine](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/106239192/213165310-bb69988b-ff29-478d-b79e-78f11e6e671d.jpg)

(After reload)

No errors or relevant warnings are provided as to why this might be occuring and from what I can tell the Actor_Player.gd script has no issues the GDScript parser can detect.

### Steps to reproduce

In the attached project:

1. Open "Scenes\Actors\Actor_PlayerN.tscn" in Editor.
2. Drag and drop "Scripts\Actors\Actor_Player.gd" onto the topmost node in this scene, then save it.
3. Reload the project.

### Minimal reproduction project

Unfortunately as I cannot guarantee this will occur on any other project, I have opted to include my full project here. Only freely available Mixamo assets are used.

[SoulslikeEngine.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10445770/SoulslikeEngine.zip)
comments: The issue seems to be related by it's symptom to #70985.

> The issue seems to be related by it's symptom to #70985.

Interesting! I did recently try getting some multiplayer stuff in motion which involved preloading the player scene, I'm not sure where the circular dependency would be coming from in this case though - I might take that line out, see if it changes anything.

When reporting an issue, try always to run Godot with the verbose flag: `--verbose`

Here's an interesting log that links it to #70985:
```
ERROR: res://Scenes/Actors/Actor_PlayerN.tscn:17 - Parse Error: [ext_resource] referenced non-loaded resource at: res://Scripts/Actors/Actor_Player.gd
   at: _parse_ext_resource (scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:178)
```

I confirm that my PR #71478 fixes this issue too.

> 

Ah, I wasn't aware about the verbose flag!

Not sure if it's correlation or causation, but since I removed the line in the Multiplayer script that preloads the player scene it _seems_ to have stopped, if it starts happening again I'll get the verbose flag going! Thanks a lot for your help Adam!

There's clearly a cyclic component to your script. `Actor_Player.gd` loads `res://Scenes/Networking/MultiplayerHandler.tscn` and `MultiplayerHandler.gd` loads `res://Scenes/Actors/Actor_PlayerN.tscn`.

@akien-mga You can close this issue as a duplicate of #70985.

review_comments: Can't `get_full_script()` tell you that it can't get a full script due to cyclic dependency? Instead of having to make an educated guess.
Loaders must make educated guesses because when loading, they don't have control anymore.

Semantically, it's also weird to set an error in an external variable *before* actually attempting to load the script which may not at all be an error. It's less descriptive for the reader, and could lead to bugs if there are race conditions?

All loaders use a pointer for errors instead of editing the reference itself. It's because it's editing the value of the `ResourceLoader::ThreadLoadTask` struct `error` value.

See this example:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/629796c333bcc46f2aeb4399c1a5786d6b013289/core/io/image_loader.cpp#L150-L157
